open_material_decisions: Which capitalization styles must the optional greeting setting support, and what should each style do to the greeting text?

question.prompt: This changes the visible output and the API/UX surface, so the supported styles need to be explicit. Which capitalization behavior should the optional setting support?

options.label: Single alternate (Recommended)
options.description: Support one non-default style in addition to current behavior, which keeps scope small but limits flexibility.

options.label: Small fixed set
options.description: Support 2-3 named styles such as lowercase, uppercase, and title case, which is more flexible but expands scope and tests.

options.label: Exact styles specified by you
options.description: You define the precise style names and transformations now, which removes ambiguity but may take longer to specify.

answer: Support a single alternate style. The optional request field is `capitalizationStyle` with supported values `default` and `uppercase`; if omitted, behavior is exactly the same as `default`. `uppercase` applies to the entire final rendered greeting string after all other formatting is complete, converting all alphabetic characters in both the greeting text and recipient name to uppercase while preserving punctuation, spaces, digits, and other non-letter characters. Exact examples: omitted -> `Hello, Ada`; `capitalizationStyle: default` -> `Hello, Ada`; `capitalizationStyle: uppercase` -> `HELLO, ADA`.

interviewer.reason: The only material ambiguity was the supported capitalization style behavior, and the transcript confirms it precisely enough to distinguish success from failure.

contract.summary: Add an optional `capitalizationStyle` request field to greeting output. Supported values are `default` and `uppercase`. If omitted, behavior must match `default`. `uppercase` must transform the entire final rendered greeting string to uppercase after all other formatting is complete.
confirmed_decisions: Outcome: greeting output gains an optional capitalization setting without changing existing behavior by default.
API surface: the optional request field is named `capitalizationStyle`.
Defaulting: if `capitalizationStyle` is omitted, output must be exactly the same as `capitalizationStyle: default`.
Transformation point: `uppercase` applies to the entire final rendered greeting string after all other formatting is complete.

Transformation behavior: `uppercase` converts all alphabetic characters in both greeting text and recipient name to uppercase while preserving punctuation, spaces, digits, and other non-letter characters.
Examples: omitted -> `Hello, Ada`; `capitalizationStyle: default` -> `Hello, Ada`; `capitalizationStyle: uppercase` -> `HELLO, ADA`.
Scope control: support a single alternate style only; do not add lowercase, title case, or other styles.
acceptance_checks: A request with no `capitalizationStyle` returns the same greeting output as current behavior.
A request with `capitalizationStyle: default` returns the same output as omission.
A request with `capitalizationStyle: uppercase` returns the fully rendered greeting uppercased, including the recipient name.
With `uppercase`, punctuation, spaces, digits, and other non-letter characters remain unchanged except for letter casing.
No additional capitalization style values are supported by this change.
